impeach /ɪmˈpiːtʃ/
verb
past tense: impeached; past participle: impeached
  1. (used about a court of law, especially in the US and some other countries) to officially accuse a public official of committing a serious crime while they are still in office
    महाभियोग लगाना
    "the president was impeached for lying to the congress about the events of that year"
  2. to call into question the integrity or validity of something, especially the honesty of a person who is giving evidence

People also ask

  • What does it mean to impeach a president?
  • How many presidents have been impeached?
